lower_bound.quote:
Indeed, since all primes are at least $2$,
\[
2^{|D|}\le w(D\setminus\{p\})<a_1
\]
for the corresponding $p$.
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: take $a_1=2$. Then the accepted integers are exactly the even integers, so $\mathcal C=\{\{2\}\}$. For the terminal member $D=\{2\}$ and $p=2$, one has $w(D\setminus\{p\})=w(\varnothing)=1$, whereas $2^{|D|}=2$, so the asserted inequality $2\le1$ is false.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This inequality is the written justification that terminal members have bounded cardinality. That bound is then used with Lemma 1 to prove finitely many terminal members, hence finiteness of $P$ and $\mathcal C$.

parsed.notes: The characterization and periodicity assembly are fully written. The finiteness argument contains a false exponent: only $2^{|D|-1}\le w(D\setminus\{p\})$ follows. Although easily repairable, that repair is not written.
